capabilities.detail: Native desktop OS and bundled Chromium only; reduced or exact runtime UA. Headers/low/high-entropy hints must be observed. No cross-OS identity.
Supported context options; diagnosed in the actual page.
Validated persistent context options; dimensions and DPR are measured.
Explicit coordinates and permission required. Read granted coordinates with a bounded call; denied without configured consent.
Read actual navigator values; no arbitrary hardware/platform override.
Report native masked/unmasked vendor and renderer when permitted; no vendor/noise spoofing.
Hash controlled native samples; no injected noise or randomized output.
Generic-family metrics only, not an installed-font inventory or a spoofed font set.
Experimental requested Chromium policy, not a UDP firewall. Controlled Linux loopback STUN still sends UDP; no candidate addresses in production diagnostics, public STUN/TURN or leak certification.
Observe permission states and device-kind counts without getUserMedia; no names, device IDs or identity spoofing.
Observed runtime availability. No masking of webdriver or removal of fundamental browser protections.
Requires opt-in controlled external authoritative DNS infrastructure; local checks/public-IP probes are insufficient.

limitations: Native hardware/graphics/canvas/audio/font/media behavior is measured, not spoofed
Canvas/audio hashes and native details are fingerprint identifiers: keep local diagnostic data private
Local ICE uses no STUN/TURN and records no candidate addresses; public DNS/WebRTC leak protection is not certified
The requested UDP policy is not a firewall: Linux loopback STUN still sent UDP with an HTTP proxy; public/Windows STUN behavior remains unverified
Client hints and permission policies can be unavailable on insecure or restricted origins; unavailable is not a successful verification
